messages:
tess: Heads-up — OrionPay reporting repeated 429s + 2–3s tail latency spikes. Their dedicated pool is bouncing between 2 and 6 replicas. Customer opened a support ticket and wants a mitigation asap.
ryan: Copy. I see matching autoscaler events in the last 18m. queue_length jumps then almost immediately drops, scaler shrinks, then load spikes again -> churn. Posting graph: https://metrics.redwood.example/graph/pool/orionpay
autoscaler-bot: Alert: rapid_scale_events for pool=orionpay (count=8 in 15m). configured_min_cooldown=60s, observed_inter_event=~35s.
maria: Can you paste the decision log + the tenant id? need repro steps to show to customer. Also did billing spikes show anything unusual?
tess: tenant=orionpay-prod-42. Billing looks normal. Decision log snippet: ```
[2026-06-12T02:12:11Z] queue_len=120, avg_lat=420ms -> scale_up to 4
[2026-06-12T02:12:46Z] queue_len=10, avg_lat=180ms -> scale_down to 2
[2026-06-12T02:13:20Z] queue_len=110, avg_lat=500ms -> scale_up to 6
[2026-06-12T02:14:00Z] queue_len=8, avg_lat=200ms -> scale_down to 3
```
ryan: Looks like very spiky short bursts from a tenant-level batch job. Autoscaler reacting to instantaneous queue_len without smoothing. Could be noisy neighbor behavior — one tenant's job floods the queue for 30–45s then ends.
neil: Agreed. Quick mitigation options: 1) increase cooldown to 300s for orionpay pool, 2) add short smoothing window (e.g., 60s moving avg) to the queue_len metric, 3) enforce per-tenant concurrency cap so a single job can't saturate all workers.
julie: Please escalate to Support so customer knows we're on it. @orionpay-cs: we'll apply mitigations and follow up with a timeline.
ryan: I'll apply the emergency cooldown and enable smoothing on the scaler config. Command: `redwoodctl pools update --pool orionpay --min-cooldown 300s --smoothing-window 60s`
autoscaler-bot: Change requested by ryan: will schedule rolling config update to pool=orionpay. ETA ~2m.
tess: After the change I can ask the customer to re-run their job. Can we also pin a warm replica (warmup_count=1) to lower cold-start spikes?
neil: Good idea. Add `warmup_count=1` and set a max_scale=8 to limit runaway scale. Also open a follow-up task to add proportional damping to the scaler (alpha=0.6) so scale_down is less aggressive.
maria: Filing the repro ticket and attaching the logs. I'll include the `redwoodctl` commands and the graph. Ticket #SUP-81233.
ryan: Config applied and rolled to pool (confirmed). Monitoring for 15m.
tess: Customer re-ran the batch. Initial results: no 429s during run, average latency stable ~220ms. Asking customer to validate over next 24h.
julie: Noted. Can someone create a short postmortem if this recurs? Customer expects a root cause write-up.
neil: Will lead the postmortem if we see recurrence. For now action items: (1) emergency cooldown + smoothing (done), (2) warm replica + max_scale cap (done), (3) follow-up engineering ticket to add proportional damping and per-tenant concurrency caps.
ryan: Adding tickets to sprint and pinging eng-runtime.
tess: Thanks team — will update customer and close the support loop once they confirm. :thumbsup:
ryan: closing here for now, will re-open if churn returns. done.
